images.caption: Bracken mowing, Porth Hellick On the strip of land (a vegetated sand and shingle bar) between the bay and the Porth Hellick Pool in the Higher Moors Nature Trail. The mowing may be to attempt to suppress the bracken and allow the grass and wild flowers to return as is being done on The Garrison by Dartmoor ponies.

images.filename: Chambered Cairn, Porth Hellick Down, St. Mary's - geograph.org.uk - 934767.jpg
images.caption: Chambered Cairn, Porth Hellick Down, St. Mary's One of seven "other" chambered cairns in the area in addition to the famous large cairn. The eight form a cemetery or group of family shrines. They were probably built about 2000-1500 BC on unenclosed land beside the coast.

images.filename: Lichen-zoned Rock, Porth Hellick, Scilly - geograph.org.uk - 1479990.jpg
images.caption: Lichen-zoned Rock, Porth Hellick, Scilly This boulder shows a beautiful zonation of lichens, with the yellow Xanthoria capping the rock and the black zone just below. The rocks in the background also show the thin yellow band of Xanthoria.

images.caption: Porth Hellick Down, St Mary's, Scilly This path leads from Porth Hellick northwards over the downland towards Pelistry. There are many rocky outcrops and several entrance graves on these downs.

images.filename: Bosky Pine Trees at Porth Hellick - geograph.org.uk - 1617218.jpg
images.caption: Bosky Pine Trees at Porth Hellick The path from Porth Hellick heading south first leads through this curious grove of Pine Trees. The ground is heavily carpeted with Pine needles, and the trees themselves seem to be festooned with dead, straggly growths. The word 'bosky' (meaning 'bushy') springs to mind.
